_how_it_is_used: server_scripts/grindless/opv/antimatter.js makes one recipe per entry, id grindless:<type>/<name>, with its programmed circuit; 'site' true locks the recipe to grindless:cygnus_x1_orbit; 'wear' inputs are consumed by their chance (out of 10000); 'chanceOut' outputs are made by their chance; 'generator' true writes the EUt negative (a generator type). antihydrogen_synthesis and annihilation_power are package OpV-B3's machine types (data key = dataKey, the EMI line). Package OpV-B3, docs/eras/opv.md machines 3 and 5-8 and process lines 26-28 and 30-33.

recipes._why: machine 3 c1: one cold antiproton cell and one dense positron cell meet in the octupole trap (5% lost to shield-wall heat). The magnet wears 1/64; both emptied Penning traps return at 90%
recipes.name: trap_antihydrogen

recipes._why: machine 3 c2: Lyman-alpha laser cooling of the trapped atoms; the laser wears 1/128 a run, 5% of the atoms are lost
recipes.name: laser_cool

recipes._why: machine 3 c3: cooled atoms freeze into ice in one levitation trap cell (5% lost). The engine returns 95% of emptied cells
recipes.name: freeze_ice

recipes._why: machine 5 c1: fullCost = 4,195,656,183,241.116 EU (beam + positrons + loss-weighted foundry + magnet/laser wear + tile/16 - 95% returned cell). Duration = ceil(1.7 * fullCost / 536870912 / 100) * 100 = 13300 t. EU out = 7,140,383,129,600, ratio 1.70185x. Named upstream steps and coordinator-approved F1-F3 assumptions are in opv-antimatter.test.mjs. Neutrinos leave; traps/cells and activated tiles are contained
recipes.name: burn_ice

recipes._why: machine 5 c2: fullCost = 11,511,026,372,166.219 EU (8 cold cells + stacking - 90% returned Penning traps + complete pellet line + tile/16). Duration = ceil(1.8 * fullCost / 1073741824 / 100) * 100 = 19300 t. EU out = 20,723,217,203,200, ratio about 1.80029x. Named costs and F1-F3 assumptions are in opv-antimatter.test.mjs; bulk W/Re returns grant no EU credit. Spent hohlraum goes to actinide recovery
recipes.name: burn_pellet

recipes._why: line 31: tungsten and rhenium smelted into the W-Re hohlraum alloy (3 W : 1 Re)
recipes.name: w_re_alloy

recipes._why: line 27: REBCO conductor slit into the octupole's tape; the edge trim is the substrate tape and goes back to the coated conductor line
recipes.name: octupole_tape

recipes._why: line 33: the GaSb boule wafered; the kerf is GaSb powder and goes back through the centrifuge to crystal growth
recipes.name: gasb_wafers

recipes._why: line 32: boron-10 and carbon reacted into B4C-10, the absorber's neutron-capture phase
recipes.name: b4c_10

recipes._why: line 26: the Lyman-alpha laser filled with krypton and closed round its tripler cell and Ti:sapphire crystal; the spent krypton comes back (to the cryogenic plant's krypton purification)
recipes.name: lyman_alpha_laser

recipes._why: line 31: the spent hohlraum dissolved in nitric acid: its curium goes to the actinide partitioner (circuit 9) as nitrate, the W-Re shell back as dusts
recipes.name: spent_hohlraum_dissolution

recipes._why: line 33: the GaSb kerf separated back into gallium and antimony dust, the feed of crystal growth circuit 27
recipes.name: gasb_kerf

recipes._why: line 32: blend the neutron-capture B4C-10 phase into tungsten heat-spreader powder before SPS densification
recipes.name: w_b4c_powder

recipes._why: line 31: blend equal deuterium and tritium charges before the cryogenic plant conditions the DT fill
recipes.name: dt_fill

recipes._why: line 28: pressure-anneal the pyrolyser's graphite to align its crystallites before electron-beam cleavage
recipes.name: hopg_ordering

recipes._why: line 26: the krypton tripler cell: an MgF2 window, an LBO crystal in a tungsten-steel body, a krypton fill under a helium purge
recipes.name: kr_tripler_cell
